clue.text: Word missing in puzzle? It's hard to bear

indicators.note: the word Word is said to be absent from the puzzle, so it is taken out of it

parts.note: a crossword is a kind of puzzle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter wonders about a word left out of a puzzle, which is hard to put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing in' tells you to take WORD out of CROSSWORD, leaving the first five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden one must carry or suffer is called one's cross to bear.

clue.text: Diagram shows how catechism could be structured

indicators.note: the letters of catechism are built into a different structure, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A diagram demonstrates how a religious catechism might be organised.
explanation.definitionFit: A schematic is a simplified technical drawing, a kind of diagram.

clue.text: Sailor, heading off with a few coins, left port

indicators.note: the sailor word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
loose coins are small change

explanation.surface: A sailor sets off with a little money and leaves the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' trims TAR to AR. The port is Archangel (Arkhangelsk) in northern Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Archangel is a Russian seaport on the White Sea.

clue.text: The female denied hard drink gets watery stuff

indicators.note: the female pronoun is refused, that is deprived of, the letter for hard

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a female
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
rum is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A woman refused strong drink is given something watery instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'denied' removes H from SHE, leaving SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Serum is the thin watery fluid left when blood clots, so a watery substance.

clue.text: Puttin' down cake

definitions.meaning: parking a car, dropped g, means putting it down somewhere
a sticky ginger and oatmeal cake from northern England

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Puttin'' signals a dropped final G, as in parkin' for parking.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkin is a treacle and oatmeal gingerbread cake from Yorkshire and Lancashire; parking a car is setting it down.

clue.text: Island's city house not a remarkable thing

parts.note: no can mean not, as in no better
a lulu is a remarkable or outstanding person or thing

explanation.surface: A house on an island is described as nothing special.
explanation.definitionFit: Honolulu is the capital city on the Hawaiian island of Oahu.

clue.text: Money row makes one more determined

parts.note: dough is slang for money
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A dispute over cash leaves someone more resolute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like an argument, but here it is a line of seats, a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: Doughty means brave and resolute, so doughtier is braver, more determined.

clue.text: Climb having lost sight of a track

indicators.note: the climb word can no longer see the letter a, so it drops it

parts.note: an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: A climber loses track of the path on the way up.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent is the trail an animal leaves, a track hounds follow.

clue.text: Liking a word of appreciation when leading short walk

indicators.note: the thanks word goes in front of the other piece

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you

indicators.note: the walk word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a step is a short walk, a pace

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys saying thanks at the start of a brief stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims STEP to STE.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste for something is a liking for it.

clue.text: River path sure to be diverted after end of deluge

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the deluge letter
only the final letter of deluge is used
the letters of path and sure are rerouted into a new order

explanation.surface: A flooding river's course is certain to change once the downpour ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be diverted' rearranges PATHSURE into UPHRATES, which follows E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Euphrates is a great river of Mesopotamia, flowing through Turkey, Syria and Iraq.

clue.text: Success on field? Bowler maybe finally felt strain

parts.note: a bowler is a kind of hat

indicators.note: only the last letter of felt is used

parts.note: to rick a joint is to strain it

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler finally feels a muscle go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' points to cricket, where a hat-trick is three wickets with consecutive balls, but here it is the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat-trick is three successes in a row, as three goals or wickets in a game on the field.

clue.text: Second half of season with European fellow laid off in business deal

indicators.note: only the latter half of the season word is used

parts.note: summer is a season

indicators.note: the fellow is dismissed, so removed from the European word

parts.note: a German is a European
man means a fellow

explanation.surface: Late in the year a European worker is made redundant in a company deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second half of' gives MER from SUMMER; 'laid off' takes MAN from GERMAN, leaving GER.
explanation.definitionFit: A merger is the combining of two companies, a kind of business deal.

clue.text: Left inside, flap and complain

indicators.note: the left letter is put inside the flap word

parts.note: a bird's wings beat, or flap

explanation.surface: Someone left in a flap starts to whinge.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleat is to whine or grumble feebly, to complain.

clue.text: A time to imprison vile fellows, bringing humiliation

indicators.note: the pair of a and time lock up the vile fellows between them

parts.note: base means low and vile
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Locking up wicked men brings them disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to imprison' splits A and T around BASEMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Abasement is being humbled or degraded, a state of humiliation.

clue.text: Try out striker in important game

parts.note: to test is to try out
a match is struck to light it

explanation.surface: A team trials a new attacker for a big fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests football, but it is a match struck on a box. A Test match is a major international cricket game.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is a full international cricket fixture, the most important form of the game.

clue.text: Farm organised central heating

parts.note: to run something is to organise it

explanation.surface: A farm installs a heating system.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially for cattle.

clue.text: Bedtime — that chap having to mix wanted to get going

indicators.note: the letters of bedtime, that and chap are mixed together into a new order

explanation.surface: A man at bedtime finds himself needing to stir something.
explanation.definitionFit: Champing at the bit is an idiom from restless horses, meaning impatient to start.

clue.text: Description of limousine getting award?

parts.note: OS, outsize, is how one might describe a huge limousine
a limousine is a car

explanation.surface: Someone describes a stretch limo arriving to collect an award.
explanation.walkthrough: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, a fair description of a limousine, so OS CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oscar is the Academy Award statuette given for film achievement.

clue.text: Son extravagant and addicted to fashion maybe

parts.note: lavish means extravagant

explanation.surface: A son spends freely and follows every trend.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavish means following without independence, as one devoted to fashion follows every trend.

clue.text: Audibly announce the start of race for food

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: to start a race you say go

explanation.surface: A starter calls out to begin a race for something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: SAY GO, said quickly, sounds like SAGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch from palm pith, used in puddings, so a food.

clue.text: Serf with cord to fix around one plant

indicators.note: the serf word is fixed around the letter for one

parts.note: a helot was a serf in ancient Sparta
I is the Roman numeral one
a rope is a cord

explanation.surface: A serf uses string to tie something round a single plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts I inside HELOT to make HELIOT. A helot was a state serf in ancient Sparta, a word met mostly in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Heliotrope is a garden plant with fragrant purple flowers that turn toward the sun.

clue.text: Writing about place for horses and horseshoes?

indicators.note: the writing letters go about, round, the racecourse

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
Ascot is a famous English racecourse

explanation.surface: Someone writes about a racecourse and its horseshoes.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a racecourse in Berkshire, England. Horseshoes are lucky charms, hence mascots.
explanation.definitionFit: Horseshoes are hung as good-luck charms, and mascots are objects thought to bring luck.

clue.text: Ultimately you dry up, time of abstinence making you rough

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the piece is read bottom to top, backwards
only the last letter of you is used

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Someone giving up drink for Lent becomes cranky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the last letter of 'you' plus the champagne term together, making TURBU. 'dry' reads as giving up drink, but it is the wine label.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbulent means rough and agitated, as water or weather.

clue.text: Is diver itching to do this to meet expectations?

definitions.text: Is diver itching to do this
definitions.meaning: a diver with an itch would rise to the surface to scratch it

explanation.definitionFit: To come up to scratch is an idiom meaning to reach the expected standard, from a boxer toeing the line.

clue.text: Chap intends not to to keep quiet, awfully let down

indicators.note: awfully signals the remaining letters are badly jumbled
the quiet letter is not kept, so it is dropped from chap and intends

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A man means not to stay silent and feels terribly disappointed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held repeats 'to'. 'not to keep' removes P; 'awfully' rearranges CHAINTENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To disenchant is to disillusion, to let someone down.

clue.text: Revolting providers of puzzles who will cause distress?

parts.note: a people up in arms is revolting, in revolt
setters compose crosswords

explanation.surface: Rebellious crossword compilers are people who will annoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like disgusting, but means in revolt, up.
explanation.definitionFit: Upsetters are those who upset, cause distress to others.

clue.text: Mistake put right in time, slip only half noticed

indicators.note: the right letter is placed inside the time word
the right letter is placed inside the time word

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: only half of the slip word is seen, the first three letters

parts.note: to tumble is to slip and fall

explanation.surface: A mistake corrected in time, a slip only partly spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put ... in' and 'only half noticed' are the indicators. 'right' sits in the surface as correct, but it is just the letter R; and 'slip' is a fall, not an error.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in print, especially one listed for correction.

clue.text: Went on 'orse at this place — reported to be a wild beast

indicators.note: the phrase as spoken sounds like the answer

parts.note: rode is went on a horse, and 'ere is here with a dropped h, at this place

explanation.surface: A Cockney rider claims to have ridden here, sounding like a wild animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped h of 'orse tells you to drop it from here too: RODE 'ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: The roe deer is a small wild deer of Europe and Asia.

clue.text: New player may finish here after driving

definitions.text: player may finish here after driving
definitions.meaning: a golfer drives off the tee and ends the hole on the putting area

explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced; in golf the green is where the hole ends after the tee shot.

clue.text: Hospital food made pulpy

definitions.meaning: a mobile army surgical hospital, abbreviated

explanation.definitionFit: MASH stands for Mobile Army Surgical Hospital; mash is also food beaten to a pulp.
